before:
Tijuana's airport, 5 km north east of downtown, serving the San Diego-Tijuana area and its five million people. It is fifth busiest in Mexico, handling around 12,650,000 passengers in 2025.

It has a feature almost no other airport has. The airport sits right on the border and is genuinely binational: the Cross Border Xpress is a pedestrian bridge that lets ticketed passengers walk across from a terminal on the United States side directly into the Mexican terminal. Just over 4 million passengers used CBX in 2025. For a client flying into Mexico from San Diego, or out of Tijuana to elsewhere in Mexico, this turns a border crossing into a short walk.

The network is mostly domestic, 37 destinations within Mexico, with Volaris using it as a hub. It is not a long haul gateway.

One runway of 3,000 metres serves 27 parking positions, 12 of them at the terminal. The control tower is one of the tallest in Mexico.
after:
Tijuana's airport, 5 km north east of downtown, serving the San Diego-Tijuana area. The fifth busiest in Mexico, it handled around 12.65 million passengers in 2025.

It has a feature almost no other airport has. The airport sits right on the border and is genuinely binational: the Cross Border Xpress (CBX) is a pedestrian bridge that lets ticketed passengers walk across from a terminal on the United States side directly into the Mexican terminal. Just over 4 million passengers used CBX in 2025. For a client coming from San Diego to fly on within Mexico, this turns a border crossing into a short walk.

The network is mostly domestic, and GAP, which runs the airport, counts 38 routes. Volaris is the main airline.

It has a single runway of 2,960 metres. The control tower is one of the tallest in Mexico.

claims.note: GAP's own undated airport page, written from 2022 traffic, calls Tijuana the fourth busiest, after Mexico City, Cancún and Guadalajara. Monterrey has since passed it: 15,623,275 passengers in 2025 (OMA) against Tijuana's 12,650.0 thousand (GAP). The three ahead in 2022 stayed ahead in 2025: Mexico City 44,605,576 (AICM), Cancún 29,345.5 thousand and second in Mexico on AFAC's figures (ASUR), Guadalajara 18,696.6 thousand (GAP). The next airport, Los Cabos, had 7,529.9 thousand (GAP). So fifth, as Wikipedia says for 2025.

claims.wasBefore: serves 27 parking positions, 12 of them at the terminal
claims.why: Wikipedia alone; GAP's page gives the terminal 23 gates, and GAP's expansion adds nine aircraft positions (October 2025).

Held back, and the most important point for Andy: the FCDO (updated 22 September 2026) advises against all but essential travel to the city of Tijuana, except airside transit through Tijuana airport, the CBX bridge and toll road 1D and the Via Rápida to the border, and warns that travel against its advice can invalidate insurance. It calls Tijuana an extremely violent city. A UK client using CBX or connecting airside is within the advice; one staying in Tijuana is not. It replaces nothing in the old text, so it is not added without Andy's say-so.

quote: 22 September 2026
FCDO advises against all but essential travel to the city of Tijuana, except:
airside transit through Tijuana airport
the Cross Border Xpress bridge from the airport linking terminals across the Mexican-US border
Your travel insurance could be invalidated if you travel against advice from the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO).
